statement: What is the units digit of $3^{25} \cdot 7^{26}$?

choices.misconception: I paired each $3$ with a $7$ to make $21^{25}$, which ends in $1$, but forgot the extra factor of $7$ left over.
I found that $3^{25}$ ends in $3$ and $7^{26}$ ends in $9$, but I added the units digits, $3 + 9 = 12$, instead of multiplying them.
I found that $3^{25}$ ends in $3$ but thought every even power of $7$ ends in $1$, as $7^4$ does, so I got $3 \cdot 1 = 3$.
I found that $7^{26}$ ends in $9$ but treated $3^{25}$ as if it were $3^{24}$, which ends in $1$, so I got $1 \cdot 9 = 9$.

hints: Only the units digit of each factor matters.
The units digits of the powers of $3$ cycle $3, 9, 7, 1$ and those of the powers of $7$ cycle $7, 9, 3, 1$, both with period $4$.

solutions.reliable: The units digits of $3^1, 3^2, 3^3, 3^4, \ldots$ are $3, 9, 7, 1$, repeating every $4$. Since $25 = 4 \cdot 6 + 1$, $3^{25}$ ends in $3$. The units digits of $7^1, 7^2, 7^3, 7^4, \ldots$ are $7, 9, 3, 1$, also repeating every $4$. Since $26 = 4 \cdot 6 + 2$, $7^{26}$ ends in $9$. The product ends in the units digit of $3 \cdot 9 = 27$, which is $7$.
solutions.elegant: Pair the factors: $3^{25} \cdot 7^{26} = (3 \cdot 7)^{25} \cdot 7 = 21^{25} \cdot 7$. Every power of $21$ ends in $1$, so the product ends in $1 \cdot 7 = 7$.
